Florida Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar dramatically warned President Trump that his administration’s sprawling immigration crackdown is fraying the GOP’s standing with Hispanic voters, who emerged as a critical swing vote in 2024.

Salazar (R-Fla.), who spent three decades at the Spanish-language network Telemundo, discussed these concerns with Trump after she cut a stark ad arguing that his Latino voters feel betrayed and noting that half of the 50,000 migrants detained in July didn’t have a rap sheet.

“I think that some of his advisers are compromising his legacy, and I think it’s my duty not to attack — there are no attacks here,” Salazar explained to CBS News’ “Face the Nation” on Sunday.
